hindi: अथवा पण्य-भूमियों से राजा के पण्य को चुराने वाले का — “माष के मूल्य से ऊपर, पाद के मूल्य तक” बारह पण का दण्ड; “दो पाद के मूल्य तक” चौबीस पण; “तीन पाद के मूल्य तक” छत्तीस पण; “एक पण के मूल्य तक” अड़तालीस पण; “दो पण के मूल्य तक” प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; “चार पण के मूल्य तक” मध्यम; “आठ पण के मूल्य तक” उत्तम; “दस पण के मूल्य तक” वध।
english: Or, for one who steals the king's wares from ware-grounds: for “above the value of a māṣa up to the value of a quarter,” a penalty of twelve paṇas; for “up to the value of two quarters,” twenty-four paṇas; for “up to the value of three quarters,” thirty-six paṇas; for “up to the value of a paṇa,” forty-eight paṇas; for “up to the value of two paṇas,” the first fine for rashness; for “up to the value of four paṇas,” the middle; for “up to the value of eight paṇas,” the highest; for “up to the value of ten paṇas,” killing.

text_flags.why: possible: the ā is not separated by '.' here, while the parallel ranges (ā.dvi.pāda..., and ā.pāda.mūlyād in unit 9) mark it; not a change of sense

notes: Each closing iti ends a quoted value-range and is shown by the quotation marks only. pāda = quarter, read as a quarter of a paṇa because the ranges climb to two and three pāda, then a paṇa; the text does not name the unit. māṣa is kept as a unit name. paṇya-bhūmi = ware-ground, kept literal (market or warehouse not stated). Ranges are cumulative from the previous bound. vadha = death (not 'death penalty with torture' etc.). Glossary 4.9: daṇḍa = penalty, vadha = killing; the earlier remark "vadha = death" is superseded. pāda = quarter (of a paṇa) is the settled rendering; Hindi keeps पाद. Typed text has ā.catuṣpaṇa here but ā.catuṣ.paṇa in unit 9 (same word, no change of sense).

hindi: कोष्ठ, पण्य, कुप्य और आयुध के गृहों से कुप्य, भाण्ड और उपस्कर के अपहरणों में, आधे मूल्य वाले होने पर, ये ही दण्ड हैं।
english: In thefts of raw materials, articles and equipment from the store-, ware-, raw-material- and weapon-houses, [the thefts being] of half the values, these same penalties [apply].
notes: koṣṭha = store (granary/storeroom), kept as 'store'. bhāṇḍa = article (vessel, goods); alternatives noted. 'Of half the values' is literal: it could mean that the thresholds of unit 4 are halved, or that the stolen things are of half that value; the text does not say. Scope of the compound (houses of each of four things) follows the plain reading.

hindi: किन्तु बाहर वालों में — खेतों, खलिहानों, घरों या दुकानों से दिन में छिपकर कुप्य-भाण्ड या उपस्कर चुराने वाले का, “माष के मूल्य से ऊपर पाद के मूल्य तक” तीन पण का दण्ड, अथवा गोबर का लेप लगाकर घोषणा; “दो पाद के मूल्य तक” छह पण, अथवा गोबर की राख लगाकर घोषणा; “तीन पाद के मूल्य तक” नौ पण, अथवा गोबर की राख लगाकर घोषणा, अथवा शराव-मेखला से; “एक पण के मूल्य तक” बारह पण, मुण्डन या निर्वासन; “दो पण के मूल्य तक” चौबीस पण, अथवा मुण्डित का ईंट के टुकड़े के साथ निर्वासन; “चार पण के मूल्य तक” छत्तीस पण; “पाँच पण के मूल्य तक” अड़तालीस पण; “दस पण के मूल्य तक” प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; “बीस पण के मूल्य तक” दो सौ; “तीस पण के मूल्य तक” पाँच सौ; “चालीस पण के मूल्य तक” एक हज़ार; “पचास पण के मूल्य तक” वध।
english: But among outsiders — for one who steals, secretly by day, raw-material articles or equipment from fields, threshing-floors, houses or shops: for “above the value of a māṣa up to the value of a quarter,” a penalty of three paṇas, or, having smeared [him] with a coating of cow-dung, proclamation; for “up to the value of two quarters,” six paṇas, [or], having smeared [him] with cow-dung ash, proclamation; for “up to the value of three quarters,” nine paṇas, [or], having smeared [him] with cow-dung ash, proclamation, or [it is done] with a dish-girdle; for “up to the value of a paṇa,” twelve paṇas, shaving of the head or banishment; for “up to the value of two paṇas,” twenty-four paṇas, or banishment of the shaven one with a brick-fragment; for “up to the value of four paṇas,” thirty-six paṇas; for “up to the value of five paṇas,” forty-eight paṇas; for “up to the value of ten paṇas,” the first fine for rashness; for “up to the value of twenty paṇas,” two hundred; for “up to the value of thirty paṇas,” five hundred; for “up to the value of forty paṇas,” a thousand; for “up to the value of fifty paṇas,” killing.

text_flags.src: gomaya.bhasmanā vā pralipya-avaghoṣaṇam, (second occurrence, before śarāva.mekhalayā)
text_flags.why: possible repetition: the same phrase stands after the six-paṇa and after the nine-paṇa range; the e-text may repeat it by mistake
stray space after the '-' join; the same word is typed ā.catuṣpaṇa in unit 4 (possible)

notes: Printed '-' joins mark a sandhi in print; here they separate each value-range and its penalties (the editors' layout). The structure read: each range gives a money fine, followed by 'or' alternatives (smearing and proclamation, dish-girdle, shaving or banishment). bāhya = outer, outsiders (contrast with rāja-parigraha in unit 8); the exact sense is not given. pracchannam = hidden, secretly. kupya-bhāṇḍa may be a dvandva (raw materials and articles). pralipya-avaghoṣaṇa = smearing [him] and proclaiming; the object 'him' is supplied in English only. pravrājana = literally 'causing to go forth', here banishment (medium). śarāva = earthen dish; mekhalā = girdle, literal 'dish-girdle'. 'iṣṭakā-śakala' = brick-fragment; the clause muṇḍasya iṣṭakā-śakalena pravrājanam is read as 'banishment of the shaven one with a brick-fragment', the exact sense uncertain. dviśata/pañcaśata/sāhasra: the unit (paṇa) is not stated, so none is supplied. Ranges: cumulative from the previous bound (the first starts above a māṣa). pāda = quarter (of a paṇa), as in unit 4. Further typing points, no flag possible: "vā- ā.catuṣ.paṇa.mūlyād" has a stray space after the hyphen; the string "gomaya.bhasmanā vā pralipya-avaghoṣaṇam" occurs after the six-paṇa and after the nine-paṇa range and is kept as printed in the translation (probable dittography, see flags). Settled: daṇḍa = penalty, vadha = killing.

lines_deva: प्रसह्य दिवा रात्रौ वा स-शस्त्रस्य-अपहरतश् चतुर्.भाग.मूल्येषु एत एव द्वि.गुणा दण्डाः
lines_iast: prasahya divā rātrau vā sa-śastrasya-apaharataś catur.bhāga.mūlyeṣu eta eva dvi.guṇā daṇḍāḥ

words.gloss: in the work of false edicts and seals

hindi: कुटुम्बिक, अध्यक्ष, मुख्य और स्वामियों के झूठे आदेशों और मुहरों के कर्मों में प्रथम, मध्यम, उत्तम और वध के दण्ड हैं, अथवा अपराध के अनुसार।
english: In the work of false edicts and seals of householders, superintendents, chiefs and masters, the penalties [are] the first, middle and highest, and killing, or according to the offence.
notes: kuṭumbika = householder (head of a family), literal. svāmin = master/owner here, not 'king'. kūṭa-śāsana-mudrā-karma = work concerning false edicts and seals (probably forging, but the text says only 'work'). mudrā = seal (not 'pass' as in 10.1). 'first, middle, highest' stand for the three fines for rashness (sāhasa); 'fine for rashness' is not in the text of this unit. The pairing of the four penalties with the four offenders is not stated.
lines_deva: कुटुम्बिक.अध्यक्ष.मुख्य.स्वामिनां कूट.शासन.मुद्रा.कर्मसु पूर्व.मध्य.उत्तम.वधा दण्डाः, यथा.अपराधं वा
lines_iast: kuṭumbika.adhyakṣa.mukhya.svāmināṃ kūṭa.śāsana.mudrā.karmasu pūrva.madhya.uttama.vadhā daṇḍāḥ, yathā.aparādhaṃ vā

words.gram: m. acc. sg. pres. part. vi-√vad

hindi: यदि धर्मस्थ विवाद करते हुए पुरुष को धमकाता है, डाँटता है, हटा देता है या ग्रस लेता है, तो इस पर प्रथम साहस-दण्ड लगाए; वाणी की कठोरता में दुगुना।
english: If a dharmastha threatens, scolds, drives away or swallows up a man who is disputing, [one] should impose on him the first fine for rashness; in harshness of speech, double.
notes: dharmastha is kept as a title (an officer of the law court); not translated further. abhigrasate (abhi-√gras, 'swallow up/devour') is obscure here; the alternative is 'overawes'. kuryāt = literally 'should make'; 'impose' used. 'Double' (dvi-guṇam) = double the fine, noun supplied by sense. vāk-pāruṣya = harshness of speech (glossary 8.3). The Hindi 'तो' is the correlative of cet.
lines_deva: धर्मस्थश् चेद् विवदमानं पुरुषं तर्जयति भर्त्सयत्य् अपसारयत्य् अभिग्रसते वा पूर्वम् अस्मै साहस.दण्डं कुर्यात्, वाक्.पारुष्ये द्वि.गुणम्
lines_iast: dharmasthaś ced vivadamānaṃ puruṣaṃ tarjayati bhartsayaty apasārayaty abhigrasate vā pūrvam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryāt, vāk.pāruṣye dvi.guṇam

words.gloss: what is not to be asked

hindi: पूछने योग्य को नहीं पूछता, न पूछने योग्य को पूछता है, या पूछकर छोड़ देता है, सिखाता है, याद दिलाता है या पहले दे देता है — इस पर मध्यम साहस-दण्ड लगाए।
english: [If he] does not ask what is to be asked, asks what is not to be asked, or having asked lets [him] go, instructs, reminds, or gives beforehand — [one] should impose on him the middle fine for rashness.
notes: The subject (the dharmastha) is carried over from unit 13 and is not repeated in the Sanskrit; '[If he]' is bracketed in English, the Hindi leaves it unmarked. The closing iti ends the list and is not rendered. pūrvam dadāti: the object given beforehand is not stated. The pūrvam here could also be 'first'. 'Lets [him] go' (visṛjati) could be 'dismisses/releases'.
lines_deva: पृच्छ्यं न पृच्छति, अपृच्छ्यं पृच्छति, पृष्ट्वा वा विसृजति, शिक्षयति, स्मारयति, पूर्वं ददाति वा, इति मध्यमम् अस्मै साहस.दण्डं कुर्यात्
lines_iast: pṛcchyaṃ na pṛcchati, apṛcchyaṃ pṛcchati, pṛṣṭvā vā visṛjati, śikṣayati, smārayati, pūrvaṃ dadāti vā, iti madhyamam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryāt

words.gloss: deya (literally "to be given"; sense of deya deśa unclear, left untranslated)
adeya (literally "not to be given"; left untranslated)
by an adeśa (literally "non-deśa"; obscure, left untranslated)

hindi: देय देश को नहीं पूछता, अदेय देश को पूछता है, कार्य को अदेश से पार करा देता है, छल से पार ले जाता है, काल-हरण से थके हुए को हटवा देता है, मार्ग में आए हुए कथन को क्रम से बाहर कर देता है, साक्षियों को मति की सहायता देता है, तारित और अनुशिष्ट कार्य को फिर से ग्रहण कर लेता है — इस पर उत्तम साहस-दण्ड लगाए।
english: [If he] does not ask the deya deśa, asks the adeya deśa, carries the matter beyond by an adeśa, by trickery carries [it] over, by delay has the wearied one taken away, throws out of order the statement that has entered the track, gives the witnesses help of mind, [or] takes up again a matter that has been carried through and directed — [one] should impose on him the highest fine for rashness.
notes: Subject carried from unit 13 (the dharmastha). Several terms are obscure and rendered literally with the doubt noted: deya/adeya deśa (deśa = place, region, point; the sense of 'to be given'/'not to be given' deśa is not clear and is left untranslated); adeśena ativāhayati (possibly 'delays/diverts the case by a wrong place or direction'); chalena atiharati (object not stated; '[it]' is supplied in English; the Hindi gives 'पार ले जाता है'); kāla-haraṇa = literally 'taking away of time', i.e. delay; apavāhayati = has carried off / turns away; mārga-āpanna vākya = a statement that has come upon the track (possibly 'a statement in due course'); mati-sāhāyya = help of mind (prompting); tārita-anuśiṣṭa = carried through (concluded?) and directed; tārita may mean 'concluded/decided'. 'punar api' read as 'again'.
lines_deva: देयं देशं न पृच्छति, अदेयं देशं पृच्छति, कार्यम् अदेशेन-अतिवाहयति, छलेन-अतिहरति, काल.हरणेन श्रान्तम् अपवाहयति, मार्ग.आपन्नं वाक्यम् उत्क्रमयति, मति.साहाय्यं साक्षिभ्यो ददाति, तारित.अनुशिष्टं कार्यं पुनर् अपि गृह्णाति, उत्तमम् अस्मै साहस.दण्डं कुर्यात्
lines_iast: deyaṃ deśaṃ na pṛcchati, adeyaṃ deśaṃ pṛcchati, kāryam adeśena-ativāhayati, chalena-atiharati, kāla.haraṇena śrāntam apavāhayati, mārga.āpannaṃ vākyam utkramayati, mati.sāhāyyaṃ sākṣibhyo dadāti, tārita.anuśiṣṭaṃ kāryaṃ punar api gṛhṇāti, uttamam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryāt

hindi: फिर अपराध करने पर दुगुना और स्थान से हटाना।
english: In a repeated offence, double [the penalty], and removal from the position.
notes: punar-aparādha = literally 'again-offence', repeated offence. vyavaropaṇa = literally 'uprooting', removal. sthāna = position, place (office). 'Double' with the fine understood; bracketed in English only.
lines_deva: पुनर्.अपराधे द्वि.गुणं स्थानाद् व्यवरोपणं च
lines_iast: punar.aparādhe dvi.guṇaṃ sthānād vyavaropaṇaṃ ca

hindi: यदि लेखक कहे हुए को नहीं लिखता, न कहे हुए को लिखता है, बुरे कहे हुए को भीतर लिखता है, भली-भाँति कहे हुए को खुरच देता है, या अर्थ की उत्पत्ति को बदल देता है, तो इस पर प्रथम साहस-दण्ड लगाए, अथवा अपराध के अनुसार।
english: If a scribe does not write what is said, writes what is not said, writes in what is ill-said, scratches out what is well-said, or alters the arising of the sense, [one] should impose on him the first fine for rashness, or according to the offence.
notes: Closing iti ends the list and is not rendered. upalikhati (upa-√likh) = literally 'writes in/alongside'; ullikhati (ud-√likh) = 'scratches out/scrapes'; both are kept literal and the sense is medium. artha-utpatti = the arising/origin of the sense (artha may also be 'matter' or 'purpose'); vikalpayati = makes alternative, alters. 'First' fine = pūrva, as in unit 13.
lines_deva: लेखकश् चेद् उक्तं न लिखति, अनुक्तं लिखति, दुरुक्तम् उपलिखति, सूक्तम् उल्लिखति, अर्थ.उत्पत्तिं वा विकल्पयति, इति पूर्वम् अस्मै साहस.दण्डं कुर्याद्, यथा.अपराधं वा
lines_iast: lekhakaś ced uktaṃ na likhati, anuktaṃ likhati, duruktam upalikhati, sūktam ullikhati, artha.utpattiṃ vā vikalpayati, iti pūrvam asmai sāhasa.daṇḍaṃ kuryād, yathā.aparādhaṃ vā

words.gloss: on one not to be punished
eight times the shortfall or excess

hindi: यदि धर्मस्थ या प्रदेष्टा दण्ड न देने योग्य पर धन-दण्ड डालता है, तो इस पर क्षेप का दुगुना दण्ड लगाए, अथवा हीन या अतिरिक्त का आठ गुना।
english: [If] a dharmastha or a pradeṣṭṛ imposes a money penalty on one who is not to be punished, [one] should impose on him a penalty of twice the imposition, or eight times the shortfall or excess.
notes: hairaṇya-daṇḍa = fine consisting of money (hiraṇya = money, glossary 5.2). adaṇḍya = not to be fined (not punishable). kṣepa = imposition (throwing on); 'twice the imposition' = double of the amount imposed. hīna-atirikta = literally 'lacking-exceeding'; the reference (the shortfall or excess in the fine) is not clear: medium. The Sanskrit has no 'cet' here; 'If' is supplied from the construction (the sentence continues the conditional of units 13-17).
lines_deva: धर्मस्थः प्रदेष्टा वा हैरण्य.दण्डम् अदण्ड्ये क्षिपति क्षेप.द्वि.गुणम् अस्मै दण्डं कुर्यात्, हीन.अतिरिक्त.अष्ट.गुणं वा
lines_iast: dharmasthaḥ pradeṣṭā vā hairaṇya.daṇḍam adaṇḍye kṣipati kṣepa.dvi.guṇam asmai daṇḍaṃ kuryāt, hīna.atirikta.aṣṭa.guṇaṃ vā

hindi: शारीरिक दण्ड डालने पर वह शारीरिक दण्ड ही भोगे, अथवा निष्क्रय का दुगुना।
english: [If he] imposes bodily punishment, [he] should incur just a bodily punishment, or twice the redemption-price.
notes: Subject and object of the imposing (on one not to be punished) are carried over from unit 18 and are not repeated. bhajeta = should share in / incur. niṣkraya = redemption price (ransom); its use for commuting a bodily punishment is not stated. daṇḍa here = punishment (bodily), not 'fine'.
lines_deva: शरीर.दण्डं क्षिपति शारीरम् एव दण्डं भजेत, निष्क्रय.द्वि.गुणं वा
lines_iast: śarīra.daṇḍaṃ kṣipati śārīram eva daṇḍaṃ bhajeta, niṣkraya.dvi.guṇaṃ vā

hindi: अथवा जिस वास्तविक अर्थ को नष्ट करता है, या अवास्तविक अर्थ को बनाता है, उसका आठ गुना दण्ड दे।
english: Or whichever real matter he destroys, [or] unreal matter he makes, he should pay a penalty eight times that.
notes: artha = matter (could also be 'amount', 'thing', 'wealth'); bhūta/abhūta = real/unreal (existing/not existing). Subject (he) carried over from unit 19; the Sanskrit has the relative yam and the correlative tad- inside the compound. dadyāt = should give (pay). The exact sense of 'destroy a real artha / make an unreal artha' is not explained.
lines_deva: यं वा भूतम् अर्थं नाशयति अभूतम् अर्थं करोति तद्.अष्ट.गुणं दण्डं दद्यात्
lines_iast: yaṃ vā bhūtam arthaṃ nāśayati abhūtam arthaṃ karoti tad.aṣṭa.guṇaṃ daṇḍaṃ dadyāt

words.gloss: in obstructions and bindings of bed, seat, food, evacuation, movement
of the one who has it done

hindi: धर्मस्थ से सम्बन्धित चारक में या बन्धनागार में शय्या, आसन, भोजन, मलत्याग, सञ्चार के रोध और बन्धन में तीन पण अधिक वाले दण्ड हैं — करने वाले के और करवाने वाले के।
english: In the cāraka belonging to the dharmasthas or in the prison, for obstructions and bindings in respect of bed, seat, food, evacuation and movement, the penalties [are] three paṇas higher [in each case], for the doer and for the one who has it done.
notes: cāraka kept as a term (a place of confinement); dharmasthīya may qualify only cāraka or both places. The compound is read as 'obstructions and bindings of bed, seat, food, evacuation, movement'. uccāra = evacuation (alternative: utterance). tri-paṇa-uttarā: 'three paṇas higher' is the literal reading; it could mean each fine rises by three paṇas, or that the fines start from and exceed three paṇas; '[in each case]' is a bracketed supplied phrase in English, the Hindi gives 'अधिक वाले' only.
lines_deva: धर्मस्थीये चारके बन्धन.अगारे वा शय्या.आसन.भोजन.उच्चार.सञ्चार.रोध.बन्धनेषु त्रि.पण.उत्तरा दण्डाः कर्तुः कारयितुश् च
lines_iast: dharmasthīye cārake bandhana.agāre vā śayyā.āsana.bhojana.uccāra.sañcāra.rodha.bandhaneṣu tri.paṇa.uttarā daṇḍāḥ kartuḥ kārayituś ca

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. nis-√pat

hindi: चारक से अभियुक्त को छोड़ने वाले या निकलवा देने वाले का मध्यम साहस-दण्ड और अभियोग का दान; बन्धनागार से सारी सम्पत्ति और वध।
english: For one who releases or lets out a charged person from the cāraka: the middle fine for rashness and the giving of the charge; [for one who does so] from the prison, the entire property and killing.
notes: abhiyoga-dāna = literally 'giving of the charge/accusation'; the sense (paying the amount of the claim, or the charge going to the releaser) is not stated: low. niṣpātayati (caus. nis-√pat) = causes to go out. sarva-sva = the whole of [his] property. '[for one who does so]' supplied in English for the missing subject.
lines_deva: चारकाद् अभियुक्तं मुञ्चतो निष्पातयतो वा मध्यमः साहस.दण्डः, अभियोग.दानं च, बन्धन.अगारात् सर्व.स्वं वधश् च
lines_iast: cārakād abhiyuktaṃ muñcato niṣpātayato vā madhyamaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, abhiyoga.dānaṃ ca, bandhana.agārāt sarva.svaṃ vadhaś ca

words.gloss: of one who makes move about
words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. √car
m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. √kṛ

words.gloss: of one who causes to go
words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. √gam
m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. pari-√kliś
m. gen. sg. pres. part. denom. ut-koṭ

hindi: बन्धनागार के अध्यक्ष का, संरुद्धक को बिना बताए घुमाने पर चौबीस पण का दण्ड; काम करवाने पर दुगुना; स्थान-परिवर्तन कराने या अन्न-पान रोकने पर छियानवे का दण्ड; कष्ट देने या उत्कोटन करने पर मध्यम साहस-दण्ड; मारने पर एक हज़ार।
english: For the prison superintendent who, without reporting, makes a confined person move about: a penalty of twenty-four paṇas; who has work done: double; who causes a change of place or obstructs food and drink: a penalty of ninety-six; who torments or utkoṭayati: the middle fine for rashness; who kills: a thousand.
notes: saṃruddhaka = a confined person. cārayati (caus. √car) = makes move about; the sense (lets out, lets walk about) is not decided. utkoṭayati is obscure (denominative of utkoṭa, 'bribe'): 'extorts' is used; 'takes a bribe' is the alternative; the Hindi keeps उत्कोटन. han = strike or kill; 'kills' used. ṣaṇ-ṇavati = ninety-six, unit not stated (glossary 5.3 convention), so none is supplied. sāhasra = of a thousand (unit and 'fine' not stated). Glossary 4.9: utkoṭayati kept untranslated in English and Hindi; "extorts"/"takes a bribe" only as doubts. The two plain "daṇḍaḥ" word glosses ("fine") in this unit should read "penalty" (two identical w entries, not patchable).
lines_deva: बन्धन.अगार.अध्यक्षस्य संरुद्धकम् अनाख्याय चारयतश् चतुर्.विंशति.पणो दण्डः, कर्म कारयतो द्वि.गुणः, स्थान.अन्यत्वं गमयतो ऽन्न.पानं वा रुन्धतः षण्.णवतिर् दण्डः, परिक्लेशयत उत्कोटयतो वा मध्यमः साहस.दण्डः, घ्नतः साहस्रः
lines_iast: bandhana.agāra.adhyakṣasya saṃruddhakam anākhyāya cārayataś catur.viṃśati.paṇo daṇḍaḥ, karma kārayato dvi.guṇaḥ, sthāna.anyatvaṃ gamayato 'nna.pānaṃ vā rundhataḥ ṣaṇ.ṇavatir daṇḍaḥ, parikleśayata utkoṭayato vā madhyamaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, ghnataḥ sāhasraḥ

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. adhi-√car

words.gloss: wife of a thief or ḍāmarika

hindi: ग्रहण की हुई दासी, आहितिका या संरुद्धिका के पास जाने वाले का प्रथम साहस-दण्ड; चोर या डामरिक की पत्नी के पास जाने पर मध्यम; संरुद्धिका आर्या के पास जाने पर उत्तम।
english: For one who approaches a taken-over female slave, an āhitikā, or a confined woman: the first fine for rashness; [for approaching] the wife of a thief or ḍāmarika: the middle; [for approaching] a confined ārya woman: the highest.
notes: adhicarati (adhi-√car) = literally 'goes up to, approaches'; a sexual sense is implied by the context but not stated, so the literal 'approaches' is used (medium). parigṛhītā = taken over (taken, appropriated; her status is not stated). āhitikā is obscure (āhita = placed, pledged) and kept untranslated. ḍāmarika kept as printed (possibly 'rioter'). saṃruddhikā = confined woman. ārya = literally 'noble/free'; kept as 'ārya woman'. The supplied nouns/verbs in brackets are English only; the Hindi uses 'के पास जाने पर'.
lines_deva: परिगृहीतां दासीम् आहितिकां वा संरुद्धिकाम् अधिचरतः पूर्वः साहस.दण्डः, चोर.डामरिक.भार्यां मध्यमः, संरुद्धिकाम् आर्याम् उत्तमः
lines_iast: parigṛhītāṃ dāsīm āhitikāṃ vā saṃruddhikām adhicarataḥ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ, cora.ḍāmarika.bhāryāṃ madhyamaḥ, saṃruddhikām āryām uttamaḥ

hindi: अथवा संरुद्ध का वहीं घात।
english: Or the killing of the confined man right there.
notes: Genitive saṃruddhasya is ambiguous: the killing of the confined man (who has committed the act), or by him. Context: the previous unit's offence with a confined woman; the text gives no further detail. saṃruddha = confined (man).
lines_deva: संरुद्धस्य वा तत्र-एव घातः
lines_iast: saṃruddhasya vā tatra-eva ghātaḥ

words.gloss: seized at an akṣaṇa (obscure; perhaps "inopportune time")

hindi: वही अक्षण में पकड़ी गई आर्या के विषय में जाने; दासी में प्रथम साहस-दण्ड।
english: One should know just that [to apply] in the case of an ārya woman seized at an akṣaṇa; in the case of a female slave, the first fine for rashness.
notes: akṣaṇa is obscure: a-kṣaṇa could mean 'non-moment', i.e. an inopportune time; kept as akṣaṇa in the translation, and gṛhītā read as 'seized/taken'. 'tad eva' = that very (penalty of unit 25, probably); what 'that' is not stated. '[to apply]' supplied in English only.
lines_deva: तद् एव-अक्षण.गृहीतायाम् आर्यायां विद्यात्, दास्यां पूर्वः साहस.दण्डः
lines_iast: tad eva-akṣaṇa.gṛhītāyām āryāyāṃ vidyāt, dāsyāṃ pūrvaḥ sāhasa.daṇḍaḥ

words.gram: m. gen. sg. pres. part. caus. nis-√pat

hindi: चारक को बिना तोड़े निकलवा देने वाले का मध्यम; तोड़कर निकालने पर वध; बन्धनागार से सारी सम्पत्ति और वध।
english: For one who lets [a person] out without breaking the cāraka: the middle; having broken [it]: killing; [for one who does so] from the prison, the entire property and killing.
notes: The object of niṣpātayataḥ (the confined person) is not stated; the Hindi 'निकालने' follows. 'Middle' = the middle fine for rashness (unit 22). Compare unit 22; this unit restates the penalties by whether the cāraka is broken.
lines_deva: चारकम् अभित्त्वा निष्पातयतो मध्यमः, भित्त्वा वधः, बन्धन.अगारात् सर्व.स्वं वधश् च
lines_iast: cārakam abhittvā niṣpātayato madhyamaḥ, bhittvā vadhaḥ, bandhana.agārāt sarva.svaṃ vadhaś ca

words.gloss: those who go about in artha

hindi: इस प्रकार राजा पहले अर्थचरों को दण्ड से शुद्ध करे, और वे शुद्ध होकर नगरवासियों और जनपदवासियों को दमों से शुद्ध करें।
english: In this way the king should first purify the artha-caras with punishment, and they, purified, should purify the townsmen and country people with penalties.
notes: artha-cara = literally 'one who goes about in artha'; probably officials, but the sense of artha (affairs, wealth, matter) is not given, so the word is kept as artha-cara. daṇḍa here = punishment (not 'fine' as in the lists above). dama = restraint, penalty; kept literal as 'penalties'. paura/jānapada = townsmen / country people (glossary 8.1). Verse of two lines; the closing of the chapter.
lines_deva: एवम् अर्थ.चरान् पूर्वं राजा दण्डेन शोधयेत्
शोधयेयुश् च शुद्धास् ते पौर.जानपदान् दमैः
lines_iast: evam artha.carān pūrvaṃ rājā daṇḍena śodhayet
śodhayeyuś ca śuddhās te paura.jānapadān damaiḥ
